**Entry-scan mechanics.** `validateEntireDirEntries` does one `os.ReadDir` and
passes each `DirEntry.Type()` to `unsupportedEntryType`, with **no `Lstat` of its
own** — the type comes from the directory read where the platform reports one,
and where it does not, `os.ReadDir` does the `Lstat` internally, *skipping an
entry that vanished between the read and the stat*. `DirEntry.Type()` is
therefore never unresolved, and `Type() == 0` means a regular file, not unknown
(`direntType` returns `^FileMode(0)` for unknown, which sets every bit including
`ModeSymlink`, so even a leak would fail closed). Adding an `Lstat` here
reintroduces that race, which matters because `.entire/tmp` and
`.entire/metadata/<session>` churn under concurrent hooks. The entries are
checked **before** `ReadDir`'s error, because `os.ReadDir` returns what it
managed to read alongside a partial-read error and an unsupported entry among
those is a positive finding — a stronger statement than "the listing failed". One
error names the first offender in `ReadDir`'s sorted order (so the message is
deterministic) and counts the rest, rather than one error per entry: the remedy
is identical for all of them, and a user who reruns the command once per planted
entry is paying for our formatting.

**`fs.ModeIrregular` is tolerated, and that is the one place the allowlist
bends.** Windows overloads the bit: Go maps every reparse tag it has no category
for onto it (the `default` arm of `fileStat.mode` in `os/types_windows.go`),
which lands NTFS directory junctions *and* OneDrive Files On-Demand placeholders
in the same bucket, indistinguishable from a `DirEntry`. Refusing the bucket
would hard-fail every command in a repo inside a synced folder, with a remedy the
user cannot act on, and the placeholder arrives with nobody attacking anything.
The junction it would also catch cannot arrive by checkout — git has no
tree-object mode for one — so planting it already requires local code execution,
at which point this check is not what stands in the way. The bit is tolerated
only on its own: anything carrying a rejected type is rejected whatever else it
carries. Distinguishing the two would mean reading the reparse tag through a
Windows-only syscall (`FindFirstFile`, then `Reserved0 & 0x20000000` for the
name-surrogate tags); that is the upgrade path if junctions ever become worth
catching.

content.text:
You were right, and there was a second defect sitting next to it.

**The bug as reported.** `unsupportedEntryType` used `mode.IsRegular(), mode.IsDir()`. `fs.FileMode.IsDir()` is `m&ModeDir != 0` — a single-bit test, not a field test — so anything that also set `ModeDir` was waved through. I added the cases first and they failed against the old code:

```
unsupportedEntryType(dL---------) = false, want true   # ModeDir|ModeSymlink
unsupportedEntryType(dp---------) = false, want true   # ModeDir|ModeNamedPipe
unsupportedEntryType(dalTLDpSugct?rwxrwxrwx) = false, want true   # ^FileMode(0)
```

So CLAUDE.md's claim that the unknown mode "sets every bit including `ModeSymlink`, so even a leak would fail closed" was false: it also sets `ModeDir`, and `IsDir` won.

**The second defect.** The obvious fix — compare `mode.Type()` against `0`, `ModeDir`, `ModeIrregular` — would have broken the exact case `ModeIrregular` is tolerated for. Go withholds `ModeDir` only for a *name-surrogate* reparse tag (`ReparseTag & 0x20000000`, verified in `os/types_windows.go`). The OneDrive cloud tags are not surrogates, so a placeholder **directory** arrives as `ModeDir|ModeIrregular`; only a junction (a surrogate) arrives as bare `ModeIrregular`. Since `.entire`'s entries are mostly directories (`metadata`, `logs`, `tmp`), demanding the bare bit would hard-fail every command in a synced folder — the outcome the exception exists to prevent. The existing exact-equality `mode == fs.ModeIrregular` had that bug already; the `IsDir` leak was masking it.

**The fix** (`cmd/entire/cli/paths/entiredir.go:191`) masks the tolerated bit out and then tests the whole field:

```go
t := mode.Type() &^ fs.ModeIrregular
return t != 0 && t != fs.ModeDir
```

Rejected types stay rejected whatever else they carry, `ModeIrregular` included; permission and non-type bits stay outside the field, as `IsRegular` already had it.

`TestUnsupportedEntryType` now pins all of it: the two `ModeDir`-laundered combinations, the unknown mode, `ModeDir|ModeIrregular` as tolerated, `ModeDir|ModeIrregular|ModeNamedPipe` as rejected, and permission/setuid variants. The doc comment and the CLAUDE.md passage are corrected — including the "fail closed" sentence that was the tell.

`mise run lint` reports 0 issues; `./cmd/entire/cli/paths/...` passes. Note that `cmd/entire/cli` has ~28 failing tests, but they fail identically on stashed HEAD — pre-existing on this branch, unrelated to this change.

Both trees pass the named test when run individually.

So: none of the 122 failures are attributable to this change, but only the `cmd/entire/cli` set is a genuine pre-existing assertion failure on `paulo-sym`. The other three are this environment being too slow (and its ssh-agent stalling) rather than a verdict either way — I have not proven they pass here under a full parallel suite run on any tree.

**Draft message:**

```
Test the whole file type when scanning .entire's entries

unsupportedEntryType accepted an entry whenever fs.FileMode.IsRegular or
IsDir returned true. IsDir tests a single bit, mode&ModeDir != 0, rather
than the type field, so a rejected type could enter the allowlist by also
setting ModeDir. ModeDir|ModeSymlink and ModeDir|ModeNamedPipe both passed
as directories, and so did the all-bits-set mode os.ReadDir's direntType
returns when a type cannot be resolved, which sets ModeDir along with
everything else. An allowlist a rejected type can enter by setting an
extra bit is not an allowlist.

Compare the whole type field instead, and mask the tolerated
fs.ModeIrregular out of it rather than matching it exactly. Exact equality
was its own bug. Go withholds ModeDir only for a name-surrogate reparse
tag, and the OneDrive cloud tags are not surrogates, so a placeholder
directory arrives as ModeDir|ModeIrregular while only a junction arrives
as bare ModeIrregular. .entire's own entries are mostly directories, so
demanding the bare bit would have rejected metadata, logs and tmp in
exactly the synced folder the tolerance exists to keep working. The IsDir
leak was hiding that.

Masking does not soften the rest of the field. Anything carrying a
rejected type is still rejected whatever else it carries, ModeIrregular
included, and permission and non-type bits stay outside the field as
IsRegular already had them.

TestUnsupportedEntryType now pins each combination, including the two
ModeDir-laundered ones, the unresolvable mode, ModeDir|ModeIrregular as
tolerated and ModeDir|ModeIrregular|ModeNamedPipe as rejected. CLAUDE.md
claimed the unresolvable mode would fail closed because it sets
ModeSymlink, which was false while IsDir won, so that passage is
corrected too.

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Paulo Gomes <paulo@entire.io>
```
